_comment: CHAOS-5484. The single source of truth for WHICH proof receipt authorizes an enablement.
Two readers implement this rule against the same table and they are deliberately
composes SQLAlchemy column expressions and matches the operation/document pairs as a
tuple-OR; the Go reader (internal/goapiproof.OperationsWithEnablementProof) writes raw
SQL and matches them with JOIN unnest(...). Neither shape is an accident -- a
cross-product 'IN ... AND ... IN' would admit a proof recorded against a DIFFERENT
registered document -- so the two statements can never be compared as text.
They are pinned by BEHAVIOUR instead. Both sides' tests seed a real PostgreSQL from
this file and drive their own PRODUCTION predicate over it. Neither test rebuilds the
rule, so a test cannot pass by agreeing with itself, and a case the two answer
differently fails on whichever side is wrong. Adding a case here is the way to change
the rule; both suites pick it up with no other edit.
Each case seeds ONE go_api_proof_run row and asks: does this receipt authorize
'dev-hops go-api routing enable --mode <target_mode>' for that operation? Fields left
out of 'receipt' take the defaults below.

cases.name: match_edge_canary
cases.why: The unremarkable case, and the one every other case is measured against: an exact match measured through the product edge.

cases.name: match_edge_primary
cases.why: Edge evidence satisfies the stricter promotion too.

cases.name: match_proof_canary
cases.why: A shadow operation cannot be measured any other way -- PostgresSwitch.Enabled admits canary|primary only, so /query/proof is the ONLY route on which the deployed Go build will execute it. Refusing proof-route evidence here would mean an operation could only be proven after it had already been enabled.

cases.name: match_proof_primary_refused
cases.why: The load-bearing half of the mode split. /query/proof is a measurement-only handler that is never reachable from the product edge, so a proof-route receipt says the build CAN serve the operation, not that the edge DOES. Promotion to primary is promotion to served traffic and must rest on evidence that traversed the same path real traffic will.

cases.name: mismatch_fully_cited_edge_canary
cases.why: The whole point of R60. Every difference is a named defect in the PYTHON baseline, so the mismatch is evidence Go is right, not evidence Go is broken. terminal_state stays 'mismatch' in the row -- the receipt is never rewritten, only read differently.

cases.name: mismatch_fully_cited_edge_primary
cases.why: Two cited tickets, nothing outside them, measured on the edge: the strictest promotion accepts it.

cases.name: mismatch_fully_cited_proof_primary_refused
cases.why: The route rule and the citation rule are independent. Satisfying one does not buy the other.

cases.name: mismatch_cited_but_defect_null_refused
cases.why: The reason the predicate cannot just say 'differences_outside_baseline_defect = 0'. That column is NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, so a zero is ambiguous between 'computed, and every difference was cited' and 'this row predates the column and nothing ever computed it'. A non-empty baseline_defect is what tells those two apart: only a row that actually named a ticket can promote.

cases.name: mismatch_cited_but_defect_empty_refused
cases.why: Same ambiguity one step along: an EMPTY array is a writer that had the column and cited nothing. If the empty array promoted, the NULL check above could be satisfied by writing '[]' -- which is why the rule is cardinality > 0 and not merely IS NOT NULL.

cases.name: mismatch_with_uncited_difference_refused
cases.why: One difference no declared defect covers is one unexplained divergence, and a single unexplained divergence is the thing the gate exists to catch. Citing a real ticket alongside it must not launder it.

cases.name: match_route_null_canary_refused
cases.why: A pre-0128 row records no route at all. 'Any route' is not the same as 'no route': admitting an unknown provenance is the same failure shape as reading the DEFAULT 0 as an assertion. Every row in this state today is a dual_run row, so nothing legitimate is refused by this.

cases.name: terminal_state_unsupported_refused
cases.why: 'unsupported' is the runner saying it could not measure. A refusal must never read as a pass.

cases.name: terminal_state_proof_failed_refused
cases.why: Written when the build moved mid-run, so the receipt describes a build that was not serving for all of it.

cases.name: terminal_state_fallback_refused
cases.why: The edge fell back to Python. Nothing about the Go build was established.

cases.name: terminal_state_mismatch_uncited_by_omission_refused
cases.why: A plain, honest mismatch. Included so the mismatch arm cannot be read as 'mismatch now promotes'.

cases.name: wrong_stage_dual_run_refused
cases.why: dual_run is a local comparison. The gate's entire subject is whether the DEPLOYED build served the operation, which is what deployed_executed means and dual_run does not.

cases.name: wrong_candidate_build_refused
cases.why: First of the four-column controls carried over from the original predicate. A proof is evidence for ONE immutable (schema_digest, document_digest, selected_operation, candidate_build) tuple and is never carried forward across any of the four changing.

cases.name: wrong_document_digest_refused
cases.why: The control that caught a real defect in review: without the document digest in the key, a proof recorded against a DIFFERENT registered document could authorize this enablement.

cases.name: wrong_schema_digest_refused
cases.why: The SDL moved. This is the exact shape that killed the routing rows on 2026-09-01.

cases.name: wrong_operation_refused
cases.why: Proving one operation proves nothing about another.
